MUTUAL AGREEMENT TO ARBITRATE CLAIMS

This Mutual Agreement to Arbitrate Claims (this "Agreement") is between Halbrook Diagnostics, Inc. (the "Company") and Devon Achebe (the "Employee"). It is entered into in California and is governed by the Federal Arbitration Act, 9 U.S.C. § 1 et seq.

1. MUTUAL OBLIGATION. The Company and the Employee each agree to arbitrate all Covered Claims. Neither may bring a Covered Claim in court. This obligation is mutual: it binds the Company exactly as it binds the Employee, and no claim either party is more likely to bring is carved out of it.

2. COVERED CLAIMS. Covered Claims are all claims arising out of or relating to the Employee's employment or its termination, including claims under the California Fair Employment and Housing Act, Title VII, the ADA, the ADEA, the FLSA, the California Labor Code, and claims for wrongful termination, breach of contract, and tort.

3. CLAIMS NOT COVERED. This Agreement does not cover: a claim for workers' compensation or unemployment benefits; a claim before the Labor Commissioner; a charge or complaint filed with the EEOC, the Civil Rights Department, the NLRB, the SEC, or any other government agency, which the Employee may file at any time and which no term of this Agreement limits; a claim for sexual harassment or sexual assault, which the Employee may elect to bring in court under 9 U.S.C. §§ 401-402; or a representative action under the Private Attorneys General Act to the extent it may not be compelled to arbitration.

4. NEUTRAL ARBITRATOR. The arbitration is administered by JAMS under its Employment Arbitration Rules and Procedures. The arbitrator is selected by the parties from a JAMS panel by alternate striking; if they cannot agree, JAMS appoints a neutral arbitrator. The arbitrator must be a retired judge or an attorney experienced in employment law, and must disclose any matter that could affect impartiality.

5. DISCOVERY. The parties are entitled to discovery sufficient to arbitrate the claim adequately, including at least three depositions each and reasonable document requests and interrogatories. The arbitrator may order more on a showing of need, and will not deny discovery that a party needs to prove its claim.

6. REMEDIES. The arbitrator may award any remedy that would be available in court on the same claim, including compensatory, statutory, and punitive damages, reinstatement, injunctive relief, and attorneys' fees and costs where a statute provides them. No remedy otherwise available is limited by this Agreement.

7. WRITTEN AWARD. The arbitrator issues a written award stating the essential findings and conclusions on which it is based, sufficient to permit judicial review.

8. COSTS AND FEES. The Company pays all costs unique to arbitration, including the arbitrator's fees and all JAMS administrative fees, regardless of outcome. The Employee pays no more than the filing fee the Employee would have paid to file the same claim in court. The Company will pay those fees within the time the applicable rules require, and understands that its failure to pay them in time is a material breach that waives its right to compel arbitration under California Code of Civil Procedure §§ 1281.97 and 1281.98.

9. NO CLASS OR COLLECTIVE ACTION. Covered Claims are arbitrated individually. Neither party may bring a class, collective, or consolidated action, and the arbitrator has no authority to hear one. This Section does not limit a representative PAGA action to the extent one may not be waived.

10. STATUTE OF LIMITATIONS. A Covered Claim must be brought within the time the statute governing it allows. This Agreement shortens no limitations period.

11. NO CONDITION OF EMPLOYMENT ON WAIVER OF PROTECTED RIGHTS. Nothing in this Agreement prevents the Employee from discussing wages or working conditions, from disclosing information about unlawful acts in the workplace, or from testifying under subpoena.

12. SEVERABILITY. If any provision is held unenforceable, it is severed and the rest remains in effect, except that if Section 1 or Section 9 is held unenforceable in whole, this Agreement is void and the claim proceeds in court.

13. CONSIDERATION AND REVIEW. The Employee has been given fourteen (14) days to review this Agreement and to consult an attorney at the Employee's own expense. Continued employment is not the sole consideration; the Company's mutual promise to arbitrate is.

14. GOVERNING LAW. The Federal Arbitration Act governs the interpretation and enforcement of this Agreement. California law governs the Covered Claims themselves.
